scholarships.title: Hanken GBSN Honor Scholarship (GBSN Scholarship for students from developing countries)

existing.description: Tuition fees apply to Bachelor’s and Master’s degree programmes taught in English.
eligibility: Currently studying for a degree, or an alumnus, of a GBSN member school in one of the listed developing countries
Eligible for the Master's programme applied for at Hanken
Liable for tuition fees (citizens of non-EU/EEA countries without permanent residence status in Finland)
Applying within the Master's Main Admission round for English-taught Master's studies
existing.eligibility_summary: Open only to current degree students or alumni of Global Business School Network member schools located in a specific list of 21 developing countries, who are liable for Hanken tuition fees, and only within the Master's Main Admission round.
benefits: Full tuition fee waiver worth the equivalent of EUR 15,000 per academic year for two academic years
Scholarship decision issued together with the admission decision
coverage: 100% tuition fee waiver for two academic years (Master's degree duration)
Does not cover living costs, study materials, Student Union membership or student health care fees
requirements: Eligible for the Master's programme applied for
Adhere to the very specific GBSN eligibility conditions linked from the scholarship page
documents: Application for admission to a Hanken Master's programme in English
Proof that the applicant's school is a GBSN member school in an eligible country
Standard Master's admission attachments as listed on Hanken's application pages
existing.english_requirement: The scholarship can only be awarded for English-taught Master's degree studies at Hanken.
application_method: Apply through the Hanken application portal (Studyinfo.fi) during the Master's Main Admission round
Indicate the GBSN Honor Scholarship on the admission application form; no separate application is possible
existing.selection_notes: Only 2 scholarships are awarded annually. Hanken states the scholarship decision is given simultaneously with the admission decision and, under the Universities Act, scholarship decisions cannot be appealed.
existing.best_fit: Applicants who already study at, or have graduated from, a GBSN member business school in Afghanistan, Brazil, Cambodia, China, Colombia, Egypt, Ghana, India, Kenya, Kyrgyzstan, Lebanon, Mexico, Morocco, Nigeria, Peru, the Philippines, Pakistan, Senegal, South Africa, Tunisia or Turkey.
existing.notes: The GBSN Honor Scholarship is the only scholarship Hanken offers in the admission phase; all other tuition-liable first-year applicants receive only the Early Commitment offer, a 25% tuition discount, and it cannot be combined with this scholarship.
existing.application_period: Tied to the annual Master's Main Admission round for English-taught Master's programmes
existing.deadline_display: No separate scholarship deadline is published. Hanken states: "Note that the scholarship is only awarded to eligible applicants within the Master's Main Admission round." and "You apply for the GBSN Honor scholarship directly on the application form for admission."
existing.program_type: Tuition fee waiver scholarship for Master's admission

eligibility: Pursuing a doctoral degree in Information and Communications Technologies (ICT) or in an area supporting the development of ICT
Enrolled in doctoral studies at a Finnish university, or a Finnish applicant pursuing doctoral studies abroad
Has one or more accepted publications intended for inclusion in the dissertation
Has a good record of fast-paced, high-quality doctoral studies
existing.eligibility_summary: Individuals pursuing a doctoral degree in Information and Communications Technologies (ICT) or in disciplines supporting it, either at a Finnish university or, if Finnish, at a university abroad, with a good record of fast-paced, high-quality doctoral studies.
benefits: Paid directly to the grantee by the end of December 2026
coverage: One-off research scholarship of up to EUR 7,500 paid to the grantee
requirements: Supervisor must be a professor, docent or senior scientist at the university where the degree is pursued
Commitment statement must be submitted through the electronic application tool by the supervisor
documents: Commitment statement from the principal supervisor, entered via the electronic application tool by the supervisor
Accepted publication(s) intended for the dissertation
application_method: Submit an application in the Nokia Foundation electronic grant application system
existing.selection_notes: A scholarship can be granted only once to the same individual. Recipients are published on the Nokia Foundation website in December.
existing.best_fit: Advanced doctoral students in ICT with published work who are already far enough advanced that applying would not delay completion.
existing.notes: The Nokia Foundation publishes a full archive of grant and scholarship recipients from 1995 onwards on its own site.
existing.deadline_display: Deadline for the 2026 round was "15 September 2026." Applications for that round opened on 3 August 2026, so the round is now closed and the award runs as an annual cycle.
